svg.title: 2035-08-19 partial lunar eclipse — calculated event chart
svg.desc: Moon track through Earth’s shadow, celestial orientation, contact table, durations, geometry, and three geographic horizon maps. All calculated by Star Almanack.
svg.text: Disk size and track are to scale. Shadow circles show their radii at greatest eclipse.
North is celestial north; east is left. Arrow follows increasing UTC. Gold marks greatest eclipse.
Outlined disks are contact positions, not surface photographs or predicted lunar brightness.
05 / VISIBILITY ON EARTH AT THREE INSTANTS
Blue: Moon center above the geometric horizon. Pale: below. Crosses identify selected places.
Longitude increases eastward; latitude is geocentric. Maps use a 1° grid; boundaries are approximate.
These are horizon snapshots, not a claim that the entire event is visible in every blue region.
No atmospheric refraction, local terrain, clouds, or daylight suppression is included.
Track sampled every ≤2 minutes, with contact positions evaluated at the catalog’s UTC instants.
Shadow radii vary during the event; the two reference circles use the greatest-eclipse plane.
Effective Earth-radius factor: 1.010. Moon radius: 1,737.4 km.
Magnitudes measure lunar diameters, not area fractions. RA / Dec: geocentric J2000 equatorial degrees.
Instantaneous geometric model: light-time and detailed oblate-Earth shadow are not included.
Original calculations, chart design, and drawing code: Star Almanack. Positional input: JPL DE440s.
Provisional model results. Contact CSV and complete chart coordinates accompany the event page.
